Aurelion Reach / illustrated rules reference

Hero support & transit

What HoMM3 places, what the original object does, and what our current implementation gives you.

How to read this reference · scope, evidence and known pitfalls

  • Analogue means a recognisable visit role, not proof of full HoMM3 rule parity. Our movement units, spells and morale-like systems differ.
  • Pool means the adapter deterministically picks a themed variant from several sites. A painted well can therefore come from an observatory object type.
  • Fallback marks a generic replacement. The original object's special interface/effect should not be assumed present.
  • Native route uses recovered peer/channel/level data. Generic claim, repair, income and old local-offset profiles do not override these generated routes.
  • Content only means a general live definition/art entry with no source-type mapping found in this adapter. It is not a promise that the native generator places it.
  • Town ratings: quality/readiness alter strategic scores and convoy allowance; each response point adds two convoy-capacity points. Recovery relief reduces town-recovery penalties through rating thresholds; it does not heal army HP.
  • Reserve dispatch: an authored timed response can withdraw unrecruited town stock, choose a friendly destination and deliver real troops without normal hiring prices. Its flat response fee is charged; this is not a troop-stat buff.
  • Pressure guard: the response value is computed and displayed, but no applying gameplay consumer was found. Do not count it as working protection.
  • Descriptions below come from the active visit/effect fields and inspected native code, not merely the older service-contract or public-summary text. Configured fields remain inspectable under each structure.

Original-game references: 1999 publisher-hosted manual and pinned VCMI compatibility source. All displayed pictures are our existing game art; thumbnails do not modify original assets.
